convention: Image px of the 2560x1440 master (same pixels as media/rooms/gain-control-2560.*), origin top-left, continuous coordinates: pixel i spans [i, i+1). Quads are TL, TR, BR, BL as seen; for the two horizontal surfaces (gc-console, gc-model) TL/TR are the far edge (left/right) and BR/BL the near edge (right/left), so text laid on them reads with its top pointing away from the camera. Scale by (w/2560, h/1440) for other sizes.
method: Pass A: luminance edge localisation per scanline (transition pixel = max central difference; sub-pixel position from its coverage between the two neighbouring levels), least-squares line fit per edge with 3.5*MAD outlier rejection, corners by line intersection (scratchpad passA.py/passA2.py). Edges that are partly blocked (display bottom lip, right-panel bottom, console far edge) are constrained parallel to their partner edge; every clean edge parallel to the back wall measured |slope| <= 0.0012. Pass B: corners read by eye on 3x-6x nearest-neighbour zooms with a labelled 20 px (or 10 px) grid and 5 px ticks, recorded before Pass A was run. Reconcile: every visible corner agreed within 2 px, so quad = mean(A, B); hidden corners are rebuilt from the final visible corners (see notes).

gc-wall.notes: Wide dark wall display, seen straight on (edges axis-aligned to <0.1 px over its size). Quad is the outer edge of the thin (~2 px) black bezel against the grey surround; 418 x 226 px. On the right half (x >= 1046) a 2 px warm lip on the bottom bezel (rows 646-647) sits between the black screen and the wall; the bottom edge was fitted on the lip-free half and held parallel to the top. Nothing stands in front: the pendant bar ends at y~372 above it, the chair back at the head of the table starts at y~660 below it, and the right-hand plant stays clear of the right edge (max L 3 inside x 1240-1253). Best writing surface in the room.

gc-amber-left.notes: Tall amber backlit frosted panel, left of the display. Quad is the frosted glass itself, inside the lit amber reveal strip (reveal at x~609-612 and y~210-213, lit sill y~681-684, not included). One dark horizontal mullion splits it into two panes (see panes/mullionY). No occluders: the nearest chair back tops out at y~687, below the sill; the bottom rows are bright glass across the full width (min L 129). Full height is usable.

gc-amber-right.notes: Tall amber backlit frosted panel, right of the display; same construction as the left panel. The potted plant stands in front of the lower pane: its top leaf reaches row 443 and the foliage covers most of the lower pane down to the sill (occluder = conservative envelope of the dark leaf mask, closed 7x7 and widened +-8 rows). Clear area: the whole upper pane plus ~32 px of the lower pane above the leaves (usableQuad, 225 px tall). The BL corner is behind the stems and comes from the fitted left edge (rows 224-518) and bottom edge (clear columns 1394-1459, held parallel to the top).

gc-model.notes: Footprint of the lit base plate the architectural model stands on (a glowing rim on a grey plinth box, on the right end of the console). Room-side and near edges are the lower boundary of the glowing rim (rim to grey plinth face, and rim to dark near face); TL is the rim tip at the far-room end (Pass A took the plinth face edge x~1591.3, Pass B the rim tip x~1593). BR is where the walnut pier (x~1761.7, a clean vertical edge over rows 596-768) cuts it; the plate may continue behind the pier. TR is hidden behind the buildings: rebuilt through the final BR toward the object vanishing point (1197, 596), taken as the least-squares meet of three fitted receding lines (console room-side, rim, plinth base). Across the pairwise meets TR moves x 1666-1674, so treat it as +-4 px. Pass B inferred TR x 1674 from a rough visual VP, which is why the passes differ by 2.6 px there; all visible corners agree within 1.7 px. The base is only ~21 px deep in the image, too thin for text; use it as the click target and anchor labels on the buildings.

gc-console.notes: Top of the side console (credenza) that runs in depth along the right wall; far end at left (x~1521), near end at right. Edges: far edge y~717.7 (fitted over x 1523-1553 and held horizontal), room-side edge = lit top to dark reveal line (slope 0.385, rms 0.12 px), near edge y~769.8 (lit top to dark near-end face), right end = the walnut pier x~1761.6 (the console may continue behind it). At the far end the slab shows ~2.5 px of thickness, so TL is where the lit top begins on rows 718-719, not the room-side/far-edge meet (which falls at x~1516, off the console). TR is hidden under the orb stand/plinth junction: rebuilt through the final BR toward the object vanishing point; across the pairwise VP meets TR moves x 1588-1593 (+-3 px). Pass B inferred TR x 1597 from a rough visual VP, hence the 5 px difference there; all visible corners agree within 1.0 px. Occluders, in order: the model plinth (numeric: far vertical edge, room-side base line, near base line, pier), the dark orb on its stand at the far end (visual outline: the orb is the same darkness as the walnut behind it), the dark oval object on the lit strip in front of the plinth (numeric band extents plus a visual top). The free top is an L-shaped strip only ~15-18 px wide, too thin for text; use it as a hotspot.

gc-model-buildings.notes: Top-centre of each distinct block of the architectural model, left to right: x = midpoint of the block's left/right silhouette edges, y = top of its roof line (top of the bright roof cap where there is one). Pass A = per-column/per-row edges (medians); Pass B = 4x/6x grid read; final = mean. The tall tower also has a thin spire whose tip is at about (1684.5, 612.7); the anchor is its roof, not the spire. Blocks overlap (the front-centre block stands in front of the tower), so label leaders should fan outward. Smaller fragments (a white front facade near x 1641-1659, y 662.7, and the rooftop slab on the right block at y~657) are not counted as separate blocks.

vanishingPoints.note: Least-squares meet of the console room-side, rim and plinth-base lines. The scene-level lines (floor light lines, ceiling coves) do not converge cleanly (pairwise meets x 892-1185, y 497-666; this is a generated render) and the console line misses them by ~85 px. So the hidden corners use the console's own lines, not a room VP.
